- When sentiment is low (≤0.27) or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- After a price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +2–5% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- For 30d forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model often fails to reflect it; adjust downward by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.53/0.27), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days or use 7-day weighted average for smoothing.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days), model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 30d horizon.
- For 30d forecasts, if sentiment is high and price is rising, model often overestimates; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent 7-day high.
